instrument.state: A set of observations can plausibly be explained by more than one underlying mechanism or condition.
instrument.operation: Generate multiple candidate explanations, gather or inspect evidence that bears differently on them, and repeatedly revise their relative plausibility as evidence accumulates.
instrument.signal: New observations create a pattern of support, contradiction, or non-discrimination across the competing explanations.
instrument.inference: Explanations can be reprioritized, eliminated, or retained, narrowing the plausible set without requiring an early commitment to a single cause.
instrument.limit: The result is constrained by which hypotheses were generated, the quality and independence of the evidence, test sensitivity and specificity, and susceptibility to anchoring, premature closure, base-rate neglect, or confirmation bias.

target.question: What sequence of revision and assembly best explains the surviving novel draft, and which claims remain uncertain?
evidence: Synthetic manuscript inquiry: witnesses, visible variants, joins, paper features and dated correspondence support several revision/assembly accounts. A visibly overwritten patch may preserve erased ink; ordinary reading does not reveal it. No prior reading or unique chronology is stipulated.

An available bounded micro-probe elicits a localized response from a particular erased ink component. Its sensitivity range, blanks, known positives, interfering materials and possible damage to later analysis are documented in target evidence. Responsive location is only presumptive material detection; it is not proof of a particular former reading, author or date.

A separate already supplied overlay relation establishes that any detected underlayer at this patch precedes its visible overwriting. Independent collation is available to investigate a recovered reading; only independently justified correspondence can date it. Each procedure has the same access to the probe, witnesses and controls. The budget permits a control-checked patch assay and one adjacent-patch or witness follow-up.

mapping.state: Diagnose the manuscript as a stratified patient: lexical lesions are symptoms and rival formation histories are etiologies. Operational target state: Several revision/assembly explanations account for unusual phrases, visible deletions and manuscript joins. Decomposition: Ordinary revision accounts and witness comparisons.
mapping.operation: List competing revision accounts; compare visible variants, material features and dated correspondence, and weaken accounts inconsistent with those observations. Next inquiry: Collate another witness or inspect relevant dated correspondence, retaining unresolved accounts.
mapping.signal: Compatibility and conflict between the accounts and ordinary manuscript evidence.
mapping.inference: The observations constrain candidate revision sequences; an unusual phrase is not itself proof of a hidden prior state.
mapping.limit: Missing witnesses, shared copying and ambiguous material dating limit sequence claims.
